relevance_note: Single case report of a man with Tangier disease confirmed by gene sequencing: "adenosine triphosphate–binding cassette transporter gene sequencing that established the diagnosis of Tangier disease".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). His siblings are mentioned only as advised to undergo evaluation (no individual-level facts, not tested or affected as described), so they get no rows. The gene is named only as the 'adenosine triphosphate–binding cassette transporter gene' (the symbol ABCA1 is not printed in the text; reference titles say 'ABC1'); no variant description, zygosity or inheritance is printed, so one variant row is kept with variant_original_string 'not reported'. Zygosity left 'not reported' even though the paper calls the disease autosomal recessive and discusses homozygotes in general. Apolipoprotein A-1 60 mg/dL and total cholesterol 85 mg/dL are given as values but not characterised as low by the paper, so 'low apolipoprotein A-I' is 'not reported' and no total-cholesterol feature row was made. Intestinal xanthomatosis/foamy macrophages (colon, duodenum) mapped to the checklist item 'intestinal mucosal lipid deposits' as observed. Normal colonoscopic appearance is a whole-investigation finding and is recorded as the paper words it (excluding only abnormal endoscopic appearance), per D-27. Age 52 is the age at presentation/report; no explicit age at diagnosis or at onset (diarrhea 'for the past 15 years') is printed, so those are 'not reported'. Patient-denied symptoms (bleeding, abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, weight loss, fever/chills) recorded as excluded. No contradictions found.
